entry.title: How Much VRAM Do You *Actually* Need for Local LLMs?
entry.summary: TL;DR: VRAM matters more than GPU power. Most people overestimate what they need—and underestimate what actually runs well. If you’ve tried running models locally (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, etc.), you’ve probably asked: “Can my GPU run this model?” “Why does it technically load but run painfully slow?” “Do I need 24GB VRAM for everything?” The answers online are inconsistent. So instead of relying on benchmarks, I started tracking what actually works in real setups. If it doesn’t fit comfortably in VRAM, it doesn’t really “run”. Yes, you can offload to CPU or swap memory—but the experience quickly degrades. Here’s a simplified version of what consistently works: 7B models (quantized) Good for: basic chat light coding help Limitations: struggles with longer context slower responses 7B → very smooth 13B → usable but sometimes tight 👉 This is where most consumer GPUs sit. 13B → comfortable 34B → possible with quantization 👉 This is the sweet spot for serious local use 34B → usable 70B → technically possible, but often inefficient 👉 At this level, cloud often makes more sense unless you specifically need local. A faster GPU doesn’t help if the model barely fits. Q4 vs Q5 can be the difference between: “runs fine” “completely unusable” In many real-world setups: 13B models feel better than 70B simply because they’re faster and more responsive If you’re deciding today: Casual use → 7B Daily use / coding / workflows → 13B Larger than that → consider cloud I’ve been collecting patterns from: community setups repeated VRAM constraints consistent performance ranges 👉 Dataset (still evolving): https://github.com/airdropkalami/awesome-gpu-for-llm If you want deeper guides: https://bestgpuforllm.com/articles/how-much-vram-for-llm/ https://bestgpuforllm.com/articles/best-gpu-for-ollama/ Most people don’t need a bigger GPU. They need: the right model size the right quantization and realistic expectations If you’re running local LLMs, what GPU + model combo has worked best for you?
